en.title: Keeper's Diary — First Shift
en.text: First shift today. Two hundred and nineteen lamps in the suburbs alone. The foreman says a lamp out is a street forgot. I intend to be remembered as the man who never let the street be forgot. Order 1 logged.

en.title: Keeper's Diary — The Night It Went Out
en.text: The outage was scheduled for one hour. At 23:00 the feeders held. At 23:40 they were drinking. I have kept lamps forty years; I know the sound a transformer makes when it is full, and the grid sounds full tonight, and every lamp in the city is dark. Something else is lit.

en.title: Keeper's Diary — Backwards
en.text: Decided. The drinker finds the grid through the lamps that can burn; a dismantled lamp is a door walled shut. Order 14,208: dismantle 219, suburbs, transformer to the center. I kept the light for forty years. Now I keep it backwards. Forgive me, streets.

en.title: Manya's Notebook — The Fed
en.text: Three of them came to the pond again. The tall one that was the postman stands apart; he is ashamed. I put the bowl on the ice and I said their names out loud, all of them. They stood still when I said them. They remember. The light remembers too — that is why I keep my lamp.
